title: The add-slot command discarded the stored credential version on every transaction Err, also on a commit of unknown outcome, so a committed slot could be left without its credential
resolution: The command keeps the version on unavailable with the outcome unknown, for the 12d sweep, and discards it only when the transaction surely did not commit; a test with a lost commit reply fails before the fix; design, spec delta, and contract updated.

title: The placement selected a slot for the slot request's project without comparing it with the lineage's project, which the reservation records, so a task could reserve a slot allowed only for another project
resolution: placeInTransaction refuses with invalid, before the selection, a slot request whose project differs from the lineage's project; a test checks that no assignment, outbox command, or slot write follows and fails before the fix (placed); design decision 7, the spec delta, and both contracts say so.

title: The account_slots checks did not repeat the record invariant of distinct allowed projects, so a stored row with a project twice failed every later read
resolution: The allowed_projects check also calls the immutable function account_slot_distinct_projects, which refuses a repeated project, a NULL, and a second dimension; the migration test inserts each and fails before the fix on the repeated project, and the down migration drops the function.

title: The PostgreSQL race tests of the slot limit and the last slot unit also passed when the two transactions ran one after the other, so they proved no race and no serialization retry
resolution: Both race tests run each racer through a gated store whose first attempt waits after the count or held-units read until both racers read, and assert that the losing command ran at least two attempts; the resource admission test is gated the same way.
